topics.inclusion_rule: Speech, tone or articulation decoders that record scalp EEG together with surface EMG and combine the two inside one model; the design value is the fusion form named in the full text (cross-modal or bidirectional attention, feature concatenation, late or decision-level fusion), and studies that record EMG only as an EEG artifact are counted separately. Boundary: non-speech EEG-EMG fusion (limb movement), reviews and datasets without decoding are excluded from the usual-approach reading but stay in the pattern-match population; versions of one study count once.
topics.pattern: ledger modalities name both scalp_eeg and surface_emg
topics.design_field: full-text design regexes: bidirectional_cross_attention, feature_concatenation, late_or_decision_fusion, emg_as_eeg_artifact
topics.metric: Accuracy or CER of the fused decoder against single-modality and concatenation baselines.
topics.note: Replaces the prep topic cross-attention-eeg-emg-fusion, whose pattern matched only the target and gave no usual approach.

topics.inclusion_rule: Neural signal speech or tone decoding studies that shrink the recording set for the main experiment by ranking channels with trained-model attention weights (or similar attribution) and keeping a top subset, and that report a full-versus-reduced accuracy comparison. Boundary: hardware-only channel counts, exhaustive or greedy selection without attention, EMG-only electrode subsets and papers with no full-versus-reduced comparison are excluded; selecting channels with data spanning test folds or subjects is included but flagged; versions of one study count once.
topics.pattern: EEG ledger text naming a channel or electrode subset, selection or reduction
topics.design_field: full-text design regexes: attention_weight_ranking, post_hoc_attribution, search_based_selection, anatomical_prior_subset
topics.metric: Mean classification accuracy (and Cohen's kappa) for the reduced versus full channel set; higher is better.

topics.inclusion_rule: Studies that decode speech or text from a non-acoustic speech signal (lip or face video, articulatory imaging, EMG, EEG/ECoG/intracortical) and train the signal encoder against a speaker, subject or session classifier (gradient reversal, entropy-maximising or confusion loss, mutual-information penalty, or a VAE split of identity and content) to remove identity from the content representation. Boundary: GAN discriminators on the generated audio, plain multi-speaker training, and speaker classifiers used only for evaluation are excluded; versions count once; the pattern match is an upper bound.

EEG decoding studies that report accuracy on subjects whose data were not used to train the decoder (leave-one-subject-out, a fixed set of held-out subjects, or subject-independent cross-validation). Boundary: within-subject cross-validation only, fine-tuning on the test subject's labeled trials before scoring (counted, but recorded as calibrated transfer), and reviews are excluded; versions of one study count once.
